hero.filename: Borobudur as Pilgrimage Site Painting by Hooijer c1910s.jpg
hero.caption:
Painting title: "The Borobudur as Pilgrimage Site" (Dutch title: De Borobudur als bedevaartsoord). The painting reconstructs a scene of the Mahayana Buddhist temple in its heyday on Java island. Possibly in the 9th century during the Shailendra dynasty. Measurement: 67 x 96cm. The painter included two figures in white robes on the right which represent his grandfather (with a beard) Dr. D.A. Hooijer and his uncle Gijs Hooijer.
Signature: lower right: G.B. Hooijer (Gijsbert Brandt Hooijer). Inventory number: TM-75-2. Material: paper. Painting made with tempera paint. Made in circa 1910s (before 1919). This painting was donated to the Wereldmuseum in Amsterdam on 1 October 1919. Literature references: John N. Miksic, Noerhadi Magetsari, Jan Fontein, Timbul Haryono, Idham Bachtiar Setiadi: Borobubur Majestic, Mysterious, Magnificent (2011), p. 236. Publications: Koos van Brakel et al, Indie omlijst, vier eeuwen schilderkunst in Nederlandsch-Indie, 1998, p. 149.

images.filename: Lens Flare at Borobudur Stairs Kala Arches.JPG
images.caption: Lens flare at the Borobudur stairs and Kala arches entrance. Borobudur is the 8th century Buddhist monument took shape as a giant Mandala-mountain. The stairs took pilgrim from Kamadhatu (realm of desire}, through Rupadhatu (realm of forms and shapes), and finaly elevated to a higher spiritual plane of Arupadhatu (realm of formlesness). Central Java, Indonesia.
images.alt: Lens flare at the Borobudur stairs and Kala arches entrance. Borobudur is the 8th century Buddhist monument took shape as a giant Mandala-mountain. The stairs took pilgrim from Kamadhatu (realm of desire}, through Rupadhatu (realm of forms and shapes), and finaly elevated to a higher spiritual plane of Arupadhatu (realm of formlesness). Central Java, Indonesia.
